name: Formation of ACNA
description: ACNA formed in 2009 by groups separating from TEC and the Anglican Church of Canada.
narrative: ACNA formed in 2009 by groups separating from TEC and the Anglican Church of Canada. Disputes over doctrine, authority, and sexual ethics led departing Anglicans in the United States and Canada to seek a common provincial structure. The Common Cause partnership brought together groups with different histories, some previously supported by overseas Anglican provinces. The founders framed their project as preserving historic Anglican faith and enabling mission. This is their interpretation of the conflict, not a judgment that all other Anglicans abandoned Christianity.

key_figures.name: Robert Duncan
key_figures.role: founding archbishop and Common Cause organizer
key_figures.summary: An Anglican bishop and Common Cause organizer who became ACNA’s founding archbishop; his later account describes the founders’ understanding of their project.
